note: Strategy on CCR4 × CD69 — anchor on the two dense CD69- clusters: (1) In the lower (CD69-) band, two dense clusters separate along CCR4 — the left dense cluster (CCR4-) is Treg_CCR4n_CD69n (resting non-skin-homing Treg); the right dense cluster (CCR4+) is Treg_CCR4p_CD69n (skin-homing Treg, not activated). (2) Above these dense clusters the CD69+ region is sparse and scattered; apply the same CCR4 boundary: left of the boundary = Treg_CCR4n_CD69p (activated Treg without skin-homing bias); right of the boundary = Treg_CCR4p_CD69p (activated skin-homing Treg).
tips: Treg tissue-homing / activation-residency quadrants. CCR4 marks skin/mucosa-homing capacity; CD69 is an early-activation marker and (in tissue contexts) a tissue-residency marker. Treg_CCR4p_CD69p: CCR4+ CD69+. Treg_CCR4p_CD69n: CCR4+ CD69-. Treg_CCR4n_CD69p: CCR4- CD69+. Treg_CCR4n_CD69n: CCR4- CD69-. Note: CD69 interpretation differs between peripheral-blood and tissue samples — in blood it primarily reflects early activation; in tissue it is commonly associated with residency (relevant for the sister FR-FCM-Z74D_tissue cohort). In-panel co-marker priors for tissue-residency refinement: CD103 (integrin αE; CD103+CD69+ is a core TRM signature), HLA-DR (Baecher-Allan suppressive Treg), CCR6/CXCR3/CCR10 for tissue-tropism (gut, Th1-like, skin).
